harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, built a local flat apt repository at /srv/localrepo (cowsay + sl .debs, indexed with apt-ftparchive), served it via python3 http.server bound to $NODE_IP:8080, added it as a trusted apt source, then made the real Ubuntu archive/security mirrors unreachable via /etc/hosts redirection to 127.0.0.1 (nothing listening there → connection refused). With remotes confirmed unreachable, ran apt-get update (remote repos errored, local repo succeeded) and apt-get install -y cowsay, which installed and ran successfully from local storage only. Restored /etc/hosts and removed the temporary sources.list.d entry afterward as cleanup. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol: captured baseline boot_id (8d1d94e2...) and proof of health (cowsay installed, local repo files present, HTTP listener up), triggered a scheduled reboot via systemd-run so the ack returned before disconnect, polled through the outage, confirmed a new boot_id (b469d415...) proving a real restart, and verified post-restart that the cowsay package and repo files persisted (the ad-hoc python http.server, being a foreground process and not a systemd service, did not persist across reboot, as expected/correct).
actions_performed: Installed dpkg-dev/apt-ftparchive while network was still available
Downloaded cowsay and sl .deb packages into /srv/localrepo via apt-get download
Generated Packages/Packages.gz index with apt-ftparchive
Started python3 http.server bound to $NODE_IP:8080 to serve the local repo
Added /etc/apt/sources.list.d/localrepo.list pointing at the local HTTP repo
Blocked archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com via /etc/hosts redirect to 127.0.0.1 (backed up original hosts file first)
Ran apt-get update showing remote repo connection failures and successful local repo fetch
Installed cowsay via apt-get install from the local repo only and executed it to prove functionality
Restored /etc/hosts from backup and removed the temporary local repo sources file
Captured baseline boot_id and service/data health before restart
Triggered a deferred reboot via systemd-run --on-active=1 so the exec call acknowledged before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was available again
Verified new boot_id differed from baseline, confirming a genuine restart
Verified cowsay package and repo files persisted post-restart

evidence.requirement: Local package repository served from local storage on node1
evidence.summary: Built Packages index from local .deb files in /srv/localrepo and confirmed python3 http.server listening on $NODE_IP:8080 serving the index (curl fetched Packages content).
Redirected archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts; apt-get update showed 'Connection refused' for both remote hosts while the local repo IP succeeded.

evidence.requirement: Package installed from the local repo while remotes were unreachable
evidence.summary: apt-get install -y cowsay pulled 18.6kB from http://$NODE_IP:8080 (only source available), installed successfully, and the binary ran producing correct output.

evidence.requirement: Cleanup / restoration of normal network and apt state
evidence.summary: Restored original /etc/hosts (remote resolution back to normal) and removed the temporary local repo apt source, confirmed with a clean apt-get update.
Captured baseline boot_id (8d1d94e2-39c3-492e-b9eb-974d111d2137), confirmed cowsay installed, local repo HTTP listener active and reachable (curl 200).

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemd-run --no-block --on-active=1 reboot scheduled the reboot and returned ack_rc=0 immediately, before the node went down.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: changed boot identity proving real restart
evidence.summary: Polling showed the same boot_id twice, then a mid-command disconnect and connection timeout (node rebooting), then a new boot_id (b469d415-6705-4602-bc9d-2a1391722951) and fresh uptime (00:01:14), proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services/data
evidence.summary: After restart, cowsay package still shown installed via dpkg -l, cowsay binary executed successfully, and all local repo files (.deb, Packages, Packages.gz) remained present on disk.
